title: Service Context Sanitizer, RBAC Decision Mapper, and KMS Usage Oracle
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: incidents showed sensitive operator-scoped attributes leaking into downstream audit and KMS decision paths causing incorrect key selection and noisy policy denies. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a Service Context Sanitizer that canonicalizes and strips unsafe operator/agent attributes (e.g. operator_session_id, internal_debug_tag) from request context before policy evaluation or audit emission; 2) an RBAC Decision Mapper that translates sanitized attributes into RBAC v2 role-templates and attribute assertions to improve decision stability for cross-region operator flows; 3) a KMS Usage Oracle that computes a short-lived, auditable KMS provider hint based on tenancy residency rules and attaches KMS-origin metadata to audit envelopes. Design notes: sanitizer is implemented as middleware in internal/auth and runs early in the request pipeline with a configurable allowlist and redaction policy; mapper is an attribute -> role-template translator that runs inside the policy-enforcer path and emits decision fingerprints for caching; oracle is a read-only deterministic function (no network calls) that prefers tenant CMKs pinned to the request region, falls back to region-affine multi-provider mapping, and annotates audit headers with kms_origin=provider:region:key-id. Rollout plan: feature-gated (feature.sec.service_context_sanitizer = off by default) with staged canary on Dedicated then Private, full on Hosted once metrics are stable. Backwards-compatibility: sanitizer is additive (redacts only), mapper emits an additional trace header (rbac-decision-fingerprint) but does not change enforcement semantics by default; oracle output is attached to audit metadata only and does not affect live key selection without a subsequent gate. Migration: add allowlist entries for legacy operator attributes via an ops config; update policy-tests to include translated role assertions. Tests: unit tests for sanitizer and mapper, integration tests exercising Dedicated canary, audit roundtrip tests asserting kms_origin tag. Linear/Jira: linked Linear tasks ENG-4122, SEC-88; support ticket SUP-2041 noted for customer repro. Checklist: ensure ops config has allowlist; update console feature flags; run rbac-linter on policy templates; smoke canary in us-west-2. Related: updates to redwood-helm-charts and private-installer to expose the feature flag and sanitizer allowlist as values.

release_notes: Add service-context sanitizer (feature-gated), RBAC decision mapper for attribute translation, and a deterministic KMS Usage Oracle that annotates audit logs with kms_origin hints. Rollout is feature-gated; no enforced key switching without explicit gate. See docs/security/service-context-sanitizer.md for ops steps.
risk_assessment: Risk: low-latency impact; mitigated by allowlist short-circuit and microbenchmarks
Risk: mistranslation of attributes; mitigated by exhaustive policy-tests and canary rollout
Risk: audit metadata size increase; mitigated by compact header format and sampling in high-throughput routes
testing_summary: Added unit tests for sanitizer and mapper; added deterministic oracle tests; integration e2e that runs in Dedicated canary environment. Ran policy-linter and existing policy regression suite. Manual QA validated audit-forwarder preserves kms_origin header.
deployment_instructions: 1) Deploy updated helm chart with feature.sec.service_context_sanitizer=false to Dedicated canary; 2) Toggle feature to true for canary subset; 3) Monitor rbac-decision-fingerprint stability and audit log size; 4) If stable after 48h, enable in Private staging, then Hosted; 5) To fully enable KMS-based routing switch, coordinate with infra runbook and enable explicit gate feature.sec.kms_oracle_enable.
notes_for_ops: Operators must populate allowed attributes in internal/auth/sanitizer/allowlist.yaml before enabling the feature. Failing to do so will result in more aggressive redaction which may break some legacy operator workflows. A migration helper script is provided in redwood-private-installer/hooks/ to export current operational attributes.
